info.title: Sinatra API
info.description: Start, follow and stop Sinatra tasks, delegate Linear and GitHub issues, and manage workspace access. Send your token on every request as `Authorization: Bearer sntr_...`, or the access token the CLI's browser sign-in gets. Bodies are JSON. A workspace you don't belong to answers `404`, never `403`.

get.description: Owner only. Lists members, recent access requests and invitations. Invitation tokens and redemption secrets are never returned.

401.description:
Unauthorized. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_token`: The token is missing, malformed, expired or revoked, or it's an OAuth access token issued for Sinatra's MCP server rather than this API.

403.description:
Forbidden. The `error` code says which:

- `actor_not_authorized`: Only a current workspace owner can manage workspace access.

404.description:
Not found. The `error` code says which:

- `not_found`: The workspace doesn't exist, or you aren't a member of it. The API answers 404 and never 403, so it doesn't reveal which workspaces exist.

429.description:
Too many requests. The `error` code says which:

- `bad_request`: You're over the request rate limit: 600 GET requests a minute, or 120 write requests a minute, per token and per endpoint. Wait the seconds in the `Retry-After` header, then retry.

Internal server error. The `error` code says which:

get.description:
Lists the workspace's tasks, from every source, most recently active first.

To get the next page, pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. Treat the cursor as opaque. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only tasks in this status, such as `implementing` or `pr_open`. A name that isn't a task status is `invalid_status`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many tasks to return, 1 to 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page. Treat it as opaque.

200.description: A page of tasks, most recently active first.

400.description:
Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_cursor`: `cursor` isn't a well-formed cursor. Pass back a `nextCursor` unchanged.
- `invalid_limit`: `limit` isn't a whole number from 1 to 100.
- `invalid_status`: No task status has that name.

post.description:
Starts a task and returns `202` with the task and the id of your first message. The task runs like any other: it gets a sandbox, can open a pull request, and shows up in the dashboard.

Only `prompt` is required. `title` defaults to the prompt's first line, up to 80 characters. `repo` is optional: omit it to let the agent choose a repository. `model` is optional: omit it to use the repository's or workspace's model. See [Models](https://docs.sinatra.dev/docs/configuration/models).

Before it makes the task, Sinatra checks that the workspace is connected to GitHub when the start names a repository (without GitHub a task that names none can still answer, research or plan), that billing allows the task, and that the queue has room. A refusal says which in its `error` code, and a retry with the same key of a start that already made its task is never refused.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry is safe. A start retried with the same key returns the same task and never starts a second one. The same key with a different prompt, or a different repository, title or model if you send them, is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Keys belong to the person who sent them. The key becomes the first message's `messageId`.

If Sinatra saves your request but can't hand it to the agent yet, it answers `503 unavailable` with the new `taskId` and `messageId`. Retry with the same key, or send a message on that task, which sends your prompt first.

A task started this way counts against the workspace's plan like any other. Each agent takes one of the plan's running places; past that it waits. See [How the queue works](https://docs.sinatra.dev/docs/managed/billing#how-the-queue-works). It also needs model access, like a task delegated from Linear or GitHub. See [Models](https://docs.sinatra.dev/docs/configuration/models).

- `invalid_model`: `model` isn't a model Sinatra offers.

Any member of the workspace can follow up on a task started from the API, CLI, MCP or dashboard. Follow up on other tasks, such as Linear or GitHub issues, where they started; here they return `409 not_an_api_task`. A task that has been idle for a while picks up again when you follow up.

A message sent while the agent is working doesn't reach it. It waits and starts the next agent. A message isn't refused when the workspace is running as many agents at a time as its plan allows: the agent it starts takes a place in the queue, and if the queue is full, the refusal appears in the task's conversation instead.

get.description:
Returns the conversation of a task started from the API, CLI, MCP or dashboard, oldest first. A task that started elsewhere has no conversation here (`409 not_an_api_task`); its conversation is where it started.

The conversation holds final answers and questions, not progress. Each agent posts one reply: its answer, or a question when it needs your input. Sinatra adds its own notices, such as errors and refusals.

Each entry's `role` and `kind` say what it is:

- `user` and `message`: a message a person sent. `messageId` is its idempotency key, or a generated id.
- `agent` and `response`: the agent's answer.
- `agent` and `clarify`: a question the agent needs answered to continue.
- `platform` and `response` or `error`: a message from Sinatra itself, such as a refusal, an error, a stop, or files the agent produced.

When `next` isn't `null`, more entries follow: pass `next` as `after` to get the next page.

There is no streaming. To wait for a reply, poll this endpoint with `after` set to the `id` of the last entry you read, and check the task's `status` with Get a task. The agent has handed back when the task stops working, for example when it reaches `replied` or `pr_open`. While a task is waiting for a running agent to finish, its conversation stays quiet; its `queued` field says so.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `id` of the last entry you've read. Returns only later entries. An id that isn't an entry of this task is `invalid_cursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return, 1 to 200.

200.description: A page of the conversation, oldest first.

Bad request. The `error` code says which:

- `invalid_cursor`: `after` isn't an entry of this task's conversation, for example an id from another task.

role.description: Your role in it: `owner`, `admin` or `member`. New roles can appear.

installationId.description: GitHub installation id as a decimal string.

repoCatalog.description: `none` without GitHub, `syncing` before its catalog is published, `ready` once published, or `suspended`. An empty repository list while syncing doesn't mean there are no connected repositories.

byokConfigured.description: Whether your model credentials or a workspace key are configured.

defaultModel.description: The workspace's saved model default, or null when unset. Personal and repository overrides aren't included.

WorkspaceOverview.description: Read-only workspace overview, with the same member-visible data as the dashboard. No credentials or tokens.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe. 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters, with no spaces. A request repeated with the same key answers with the first one's result and does the work once; the same key with different content is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Keys belong to the person who sent them: two people using the same key start two tasks or send two messages. The key is also the `messageId` of the message the request sends, which is a start's first message.

RequestId.description: The request's id, to share with support.

bearerAuth.description: A personal access token, which starts with `sntr_`. Create one on the dashboard's CLI & API page (https://app.sinatra.dev/tokens). It acts as you in every workspace you belong to, with your role in each, and expires after at most 365 days. The CLI's browser sign-in sends an OAuth access token here instead.
